title: This 10-Foot Fish Drowns If It Can't Breathe Air
subject: arapaima

scenes.text: This ten-foot fish drowns if you keep it underwater.
The arapaima of the Amazon grows up to 10 feet long and weighs up to 440 pounds.
Its swim bladder works like a lung, so every 5 to 15 minutes it rises to gulp air with a loud gasp.
It still has gills, but breathing air tops up the oxygen they can supply.
Its scales have a hard mineral outer layer over a tough, flexible inner one. That helps protect it from piranhas.
A fish that breathes air, wearing armor against piranhas.

description:

Would you swim in the Amazon with one?
